guidelines.name: Product Manager Roadmap
orderedTopics: Introduction (what product management is, product vs project management, roles, key skills; product development lifecycle)
Product Identification (brainstorming techniques; discovery, selection, validation, execution; problem framing)
Market Analysis (identifying market needs, competitive analysis, emerging market trends)
User Research (user personas, user interviews, surveys and questionnaires, ethnographic research)
Positioning (USP, market segmentation, case studies)
Vision & Mission
Value vs Features (feature creep, finding balance)
Strategic Thinking (competitive strategy, five forces, competitive advantage, strategic partners)
Value Proposition (defining it, value proposition canvas)
Defining Goals (target, baseline, trend, timeframe)

Product Requirements (writing PRDs, user stories, job stories, prioritization techniques, grooming sessions, user story mapping) | Product Roadmap (creating a roadmap, prioritising features, continuous and outcome-based roadmaps, communicating the roadmap)
Backlog Management · Release Strategies (feature toggles, phased rollouts, dark launches)
UX / UI Design · Service Design · Interaction Design · User Testing (A/B testing, usability testing)
Go-to-Market Strategy (launch planning, marketing strategies, growth hacking)
Agile Methodology (Scrum, Kanban) · Working with Engineering Teams (sprint planning, standups, retrospectives, MVP)
Key Product Metrics (DAU, MAU, conversion, retention, churn, LTV, CAC, North Star Metric)
Data-Driven Decision Making (A/B testing, cohort analysis, predictive analytics) · Feedback Loops
Communication Skills · Managing Stakeholders
Tools: roadmapping (Product Board, Aha, Notion), project management (Jira, Linear, Trello), analytics (Amplitude, Heap, Looker), communication
Risk: identifying risks, risk assessment, mitigation, monitoring and controlling
Scaling Products · Advanced Analysis (ML/AI in product management) · Portfolio Management
Leadership and Influence
guidelines.note: Order read from the node positions (top to bottom) in roadmap.sh's own page data (roadmap.sh/product-manager.json). Product Requirements and Product Roadmap sit side by side in the same band.

guidelines.name: The Pragmatic Framework (2027 edition: 37 focus areas in 7 categories)
orderedTopics: Market: Market Problems · Product Strategy · Distinctive Competencies · Win/Loss Analysis · Competitive Landscape
Focus: Market Definition · Distribution Strategy · Product Portfolio · Product Roadmap
Business: Business Plan · Pricing · Buy, Build or Partner · Business Outcomes · Measurement
Planning: Positioning · Buyer Journey · Buyer Personas · User Personas · Requirements · Ideation · Stakeholder Management
Go-to-Market: Marketing Plan · Growth · Retention · Launch · Organizational Alignment · Awareness · Engagement · Customer Satisfaction
Enablement: Adoption · Content · Assets · Channel Support
Operations: Scaling · Exceptions · Escalations · Customer Value Realization
guidelines.note: Categories as laid out left to right on the page. «Market problems ... Finding them is the foundation for everything else in the Framework.» Its certification course order is Foundations → Focus: Strategic Product Planning → Build: Product Building Course.

guidelines.name: The Scrum Guide (November 2020): Product Owner accountabilities
orderedTopics: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.
Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal;
Creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items;
Ordering Product Backlog items; and,
Ensuring that the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood.

guidelines.name: Professional Scrum Product Owner I (PSPO I): focus areas
orderedTopics: Understanding and Applying the Scrum Framework: Empiricism, Scrum Team, Events, Artifacts, Done
Developing People and Teams: Self-Managing Teams
Managing Products with Agility: Forecasting & Release Planning, Product Vision, Product Value, Product Backlog Management, Business Strategy, Stakeholders & Customers
guidelines.note: «Many questions focus on the Product Owner accountabilities based on the Scrum Guide».

product.basedOnLine: المسار مبني على: خارطة roadmap.sh لمدير المنتج، وإطار Pragmatic Institute، ومسؤوليات مالك المنتج في دليل سكرم 2020، ومجالات اختبار PSPO I من Scrum.org
product.orderNote: Order product-discovery → product-roadmap → product-specs → product-analytics is supported, with one caveat. Discovery first: Pragmatic says of Market Problems «Finding them is the foundation for everything else in the Framework.», and on roadmap.sh User Research comes before everything about strategy and requirements. Roadmap before specs: roadmap.sh puts Vision & Mission, Strategic Thinking and Defining Goals above Product Requirements; the Scrum Guide lists «Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal;» before «Creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items;»; Pragmatic's course order is «Focus: Strategic Product Planning» before «Build: Product Building Course» («hand off market information ... so development can build the right products»). Analytics last: roadmap.sh puts Key Product Metrics and Data-Driven Decision Making after requirements, roadmap, release and go-to-market. Caveat: in the Pragmatic Framework the Business category (with Measurement) sits before Planning (with Requirements), and on roadmap.sh Product Requirements and Product Roadmap are side by side, so specs and roadmap are close to parallel.

sales-cs.basedOnLine: المسار مبني على: دورة HubSpot Academy المجانية للبيع الداخلي (Inbound Sales)
sales-cs.orderNote: Order sales → customer-success is only weakly supported. No official customer-success curriculum opened (see notOpened), and Salesforce Trailhead's sales credential pages did not open. HubSpot's sales course covers the path up to the presentation and the close, with nothing after the sale. The only line found that puts the two in sequence is from a customer-success training company, not an official body: SuccessCOACHING (successcoaching.co) «connect what Marketing positions, Sales commits, and Customer Success delivers.» Keep the order, but treat it as a judgement call.

orderedTopics: الأنظمة واللوائح

أحكام المحتوى المحلي
الأوامر والقرارات والتعاميم المرتبطة بنظام المنافسات

The ministry's page https://www.mof.gov.sa/ar/tenders-and-procurement describes Etimad: «منصة إلكترونية شاملة لخدمات وزارة المالية ... و تتضمن العديد من الخدمات الأساسية مثل إدارة العقود والميزانية والمدفوعات بالإضافة الى إدارة المنافسات والمشتريات والحقوق المالية.» etimad.sa itself only redirects to its login page.

supply-procurement.basedOnLine: المسار مبني على: مؤهلات CIPS في المشتريات والتوريد (المستويان الثاني والثالث)، وصفحة نظام المنافسات والمشتريات الحكومية في وزارة المالية (منصة اعتماد)
supply-procurement.orderNote: Order supply-chain → procurement is NOT supported by the guidelines that opened. CIPS teaches both together from the start («L2M1 Introducing Procurement and Supply»), puts procurement operations second («L2M2 Procurement and Supply Operations») and puts the supply-chain-operations module last («L2M5 Inventory, Logistics and Expediting»). ASCM's CPIM/CSCP outlines, which would describe the supply-chain side, did not open. For procurement jobs (most of the openings found), procurement could come first, or the two can be treated as parallel; Saudi government procurement (Etimad, the procurement law) belongs inside procurement.
